title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is handwritten on the back of a typescript. The text showing through is from the SGA/Pic exposé on the maximal torus of Pic^0 of a curve (pp. 470–472), which is also the 'previous' and 'next' page. So the neighbouring transcriptions are unrelated typescript, not the continuation of this note.

The manuscript sets up elementary cohomological machinery for a 'space' 𝒳. Judging from Δ_n/𝒳, 𝒳 is a simplicial set, or more generally a category or topos presented simplicially.

Part 1 ('Itou...') continues a previous discussion of a coefficient object A_x (constant coefficients) carrying some algebraic structure. The examples are an abelian group, or possibly a differential graded one. In the graded case, if the degrees are bounded below, one can form the hypercohomology RΓ(𝒳, A*_x) := RΓ_𝒳(A*_𝒳). Here A*_𝒳 is the complex induced by A* on 𝒳, i.e. the constant object, also described as A*_x × 𝒳 → 𝒳. The bounded-below hypothesis guarantees that the Cartan–Eilenberg/Godement-type resolution and the total complex behave well.

Part 2 takes a coefficient system A on the category of simplices, written A : (Δ/𝒳)° → (Ab); this replaces the crossed-out 'a group over 𝒳'. It defines the cochain complex C^n(𝒳, A) = ∏_{σ ∈ Ob Δ_n/𝒳} A(σ), a product over the n-simplices of 𝒳. It then observes that the C^n form a cosimplicial abelian group, whose associated complex computes the cohomology of 𝒳 with coefficients in A.

In modern terms this is cohomology of a simplicial set with coefficients in a functor on its category of simplices. It is equivalently the cohomology of the (op-)category of simplices, a lim^n of A over Δ/𝒳, computed by the standard cosimplicial replacement.

In the context of cote 136 (divided-power de Rham complex, IHÉS 1976), this is presumably preparation for comparing de Rham / crystalline-type cohomology with Čech–Alexander or simplicial cochain descriptions, via cosimplicial objects and the de Rham–Dold–Kan correspondence.
errors: Variance: for ∏_{σ∈X_n} A(σ) to be a cosimplicial group, the cofaces need maps A(d_iσ) → A(σ) and the codegeneracies need A(s_jτ) → A(τ). That requires A covariant on Δ/𝒳 under the usual arrow convention. Written as A : (Δ/𝒳)° → Ab, it would naturally give a simplicial (chain-type) structure instead. This is either a slip or uses the opposite convention for Δ/𝒳; it is harmless for local systems, where all maps are invertible.
The text is a fragment: no differential, no comparison statement and no proof are given.

ideas.what: Hypercohomology of a space or topos with coefficients in a constant bounded-below complex A*
ideas.modern_name: Hypercohomology RΓ(X, A*) of a bounded-below complex

ideas.what: Cochains of a simplicial set with coefficients in a functor on the category of simplices, C^n = ∏_{σ∈X_n} A(σ), forming a cosimplicial abelian group
ideas.modern_name: Cohomology with coefficients in a functor on the simplex category / cosimplicial replacement computing lim^n over Δ/X (local coefficient systems generalized)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Steenrod (local coefficients), Gabriel–Zisman, Bousfield–Kan, Quillen; folklore
ideas.where_published: Similar material appears in Pursuing Stacks (cohomology of categories and simplicial sets with coefficients) but the exact location is uncertain

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard textbook definitions (hypercohomology of a bounded-below complex; cosimplicial cochains with coefficients on the simplex category), written as preparatory scratch notes. There is nothing new or unfinished of significance.
transcription_corrections: The page is handwritten on the verso of a typescript (SGA Pic/torus text, pp. 470–472). The faint typed lines are bleed-through and are not part of the note.
'Soit A {+(𝒳/𝒳)°→(Ab)+}' should read 'Soit A : (Δ/𝒳)° → (Ab)'. The first symbol is a crossed-out triangle (Δ), and there is an overline over '(Ab)'.
'complexe induit[?] par A*, sur 𝒳' is more likely 'complexe constant déf. par A*, sur 𝒳 ou A*_x × 𝒳/𝒳'.
'on peut dans ce cas[?] l'hypercohomologie' likely reads 'on peut donc parler de l'hypercohomologie'.
Line 4 reads '- si les degrés sont bornés inférieurement -', which is correct.
'Les C^n forment un groupe cosimplicial' is correct.
